/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 20 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2791 (15)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4429 (53)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2088 (-19)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1637 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 871 (4)
CAPESIZE
The market posted a modest improvement today, driven primarily by firmer sentiment in the Pacific, while the Atlantic basin remained subdued amid a continued lack of activity. The BCI 5TC index edged up by $486 to settle at $40,170. In the Pacific, the C5 index gained $0.53 to close at $13.815. Market sentiment appeared to be finding a level, supported largely by operator-controlled cargoes despite relatively limited participation from the major miners. Trading was somewhat mixed throughout the session, with reports of a miner bidding around $12.80 against offers of $13.50, while operators were said to be bidding in the $13.60 to $14.00 range. Although there was market talk of an operator fixing at $14.00, this remained unconfirmed. By the close, a fixture reportedly concluded at $13.5 for a miner, suggesting some convergence between bids and offers. The Atlantic basin remained steady but lacked meaningful activity. The C3 route eased marginally by $0.054 to $35.605, while Brazil and West Africa business continued to be notably thin. Market participants reported offers remaining around the $36.00 level, although a lack of bidding interest continued to hinder fresh fixture activity.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market has been described by some as potentially nearing a floor, supported by growing demand for trans-Atlantic business. Meanwhile, the fronthaul market appears comparatively stronger, with increased enquiry volumes being reported. However, brokers have noted that the tonnage list remains well supplied despite the uptick in demand. Market sentiment remains divided, particularly on the P1A, with rumours of fixtures being concluded significantly below index levels continuing to circulate. Market sources suggest that longer-duration grain stems are being discounted, with both bids and offers reflecting weaker levels. The Pacific market continues to appear softer, with brokers noting that prompt tonnage supply remains in excess of demand. Reported fixtures have been concluded below the levels of the last done, particularly for longer-duration North Pacific and East Coast Australia voyages. Despite this, activity remains evident, especially on routes from Indonesia into South China and India. The Great Mind (75,474 2011) open Shanghai 28 August was said to have fixed for one year with some suggesting the rate to be in the upper $16,000's. The P5TC fell a further $174 to conclude at $18,790.

Atlantic
The LH Anthea (76,781 2006) open Gangavaram 22/23 August was said to be placed on subjects for a fronthaul from EC South America, meanwhile, the Galapagos (75,661 2010) open Rio Grande 24/25 August and the scrubber-fitted Canopus (80,992 2021) open Singapore 7 August were both said to have fixed for a similar trip.

Asia
The Guo Hai Lian 805 (81,728 2014) open Hoping 24 August was placed on subjects for an Australia to South China trip at $16,500. The New Era (82,153 2011) open Mariveles 22/23 August and the Red Lily (81,855 2017) open Hong Kong 24/25 August were both said to be on subjects for trips loading from Indonesia to South Korea and India, respectively. The scrubber-fitted Quod Verum (81,982 2019) open CJK 17/20 August was reported to have fixed, but no other details surfaced. Raffles were said to have covered their voyage grain stem from Australia and Kline were also said to have covered their Australia coal stem, both with early September laycans and discharging Singapore – Japan range.
SUPRAMAX
A familiar pattern continued with the 11TC average making a small gain of $47 to finish at $20,698. Again there were very few rumoured trades in the Atlantic today, with rates seemingly softening everywhere except the South which seems to be bucking the trend at the moment. In Asia the optimistic sentiment continued, but gains are slow and steady rather than exciting, but rates in the Indian Ocean seem to also have turned with better numbers now reported from South Africa. The Dayang Jinlan (56,469 2012) CJK 28 August was said to be on subjects for 6 to 7 months at around $15,000, but the Charterer was not mentioned, and a 57,000-dwt built 2010 was fixed basis delivery CJK for a trip to West Africa at $17,250 with a combination of clinker and generals (on deck), but further details did not emerge. The Bao Chang (56,136 2010) Singapore 30 August fixed a trip via Indonesia to China in the mid $15,000’s, whilst a Supramax was rumoured fixed at around $14-14,250 basis delivery Mombasa for a trip to China, but further details on both were lacking.
HANDYSIZE
The market showed a mixed tone today, with the 7TC average improving by $65 to close at $15,670. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, only marginal adjustments were observed, with rates remaining largely unchanged. The South Atlantic remained finely balanced, supported by a slight improvement in cargo flows and a shortage of prompt tonnage. Meanwhile, the US Gulf continued to soften, as demand remained insufficient to absorb the growing tonnage list. In the Pacific, the market saw pockets of activity, with sentiment remaining largely positional. The Iron Maiden (36,371 2014) open Cebu was fixed for multiple legs in the high $17,000's by Norden, while the Pan Amber (38,220 2012) open Phu My was also fixed for multiple legs at $17,500 by Norden, with the first leg cement to the US West Coast, but further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Shanxi Coal Output

Coal production in Shanxi fell 36% year-on-year to 69.9 Mt in July, the lowest monthly figure in eight years, following the fatal mine accident in late May, data from the National Bureau of Statistics show, McCloskey reports. In the year to July, production in the region stood 10.2% lower than the year before at 680.3 Mt. Total Chinese coal production in the same period declined 2.9% to 2.7 Bt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape curve moved higher through the session today. August traded between 38,750–39,500, with activity fairly light. September was the main focus, trading between 39,600–41,500. Early activity was concentrated around 39,750–40,250, before the market firmed steadily through the day, reaching 41,000–41,500 in the afternoon and finishing around 41,000. October traded between 41,000–42,400, also strengthening through the day and reaching the day’s highs later on. Q4
